author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dover will formally unveil a new September 11 memorial Friday, marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks with a permanent downtown tribute. The 11-foot structure, built from granite panels, stands in the Cocheco Mill Courtyard and honors all those who died, including four people with ties to Dover.

The project grew from discussions among city leaders, current and former mayors, police and fire chiefs, and former fire chief Perry Plummer. Plummer told New Hampshire Public Radio that the group initially considered a smaller memorial in a cemetery. Community interest expanded the plan, and organizers raised nearly $200,000 in private community support over the past year.

An information board beside the monument includes photographs of the four people connected to Dover, explains those connections and presents a timeline of the attacks. Organizers say the display is intended to support school visits as well as private reflection, giving younger residents who did not experience 2001 a place to learn about the day and its lasting effects.

The courtyard also carries local significance because Dover held its first remembrance ceremony there shortly after the attacks. Annual observances have continued through Dover Fire and Rescue, and the new memorial gives those ceremonies a permanent focal point in the center of the city.
dek: The 11-foot granite memorial in the Cocheco Mill Courtyard is designed as both a place of remembrance and an educational destination.
headline: Dover prepares to unveil September 11 memorial honoring four local lives
